directAnswer: You can check if your password has been leaked by using tools like Have I Been Pwned or by checking the security settings of your online accounts.
summary: Regularly checking if your password has been compromised is crucial for maintaining online security.

sections.heading: Using Password Check Tools
sections.body: Websites like Have I Been Pwned allow you to enter your email address to see if your passwords are part of any known data breaches.

sections.heading: Check Account Security Settings
sections.body: Many online services offer security features that notify you if your account has been compromised. Check the security settings of your accounts for alerts.

steps.title: Visit Have I Been Pwned
steps.detail: Go to the website and enter your email address. The site will inform you if your email or associated passwords have been involved in a breach.

steps.title: Review Security Settings
steps.detail: Log into your accounts and navigate to the security or privacy section to see if there are any alerts regarding compromised passwords.

steps.title: Enable Two-Factor Authentication
steps.detail: If available, enable two-factor authentication (2FA) to add an extra layer of security to your accounts.

faqs.question: What should I do if my password has been leaked?
faqs.answer: Immediately change your password and enable two-factor authentication on your account.

faqs.question: Are there any other tools to check for password leaks?
faqs.answer: Yes, other tools like Firefox Monitor and LastPass Security Challenge can also help check for compromised passwords.

faqs.question: How often should I check if my password has been leaked?
faqs.answer: It is advisable to check your passwords at least every few months or after any major security breach news.

caveats: Not all data breaches are reported, so it's possible your password has been compromised without your knowledge.
